title: A Daffodil in Early Spring
description: Explore a familiar spring flower through its trumpet-like center, underground bulb, and upright leaves.
cardDescription: Explore a familiar spring flower through its trumpet-like center, underground bulb, and upright leaves.
focus: Daffodil is a common name within the Narcissus group. Its central cup and surrounding flower segments have names that differ from the leafy parts below.
solvingTip: Use the location and shape in the clue: central cup, outer segment, or underground store.
words: Familiar spring flower with a central trumpet or cup

answerNotes.DAFFODIL: Daffodil is a common name for plants in Narcissus; their colors and cup lengths vary among kinds.
answerNotes.NARCISSUS: Narcissus names the broader plant group rather than only one yellow trumpet-shaped variety.
answerNotes.CORONA: Corona is the central outgrowth, distinct from the surrounding petal-like segments.
answerNotes.TEPAL: Tepal is useful for the similar-looking outer flower segments in plants such as daffodils.
answerNotes.BULB: A daffodil bulb stores resources in fleshy leaf bases around a short stem.
answerNotes.SUN: Sunlight supplies energy for photosynthesis in a daffodil's green leaves.
answerNotes.BED: A garden bed is the prepared planting area, separate from the underground bulb.
answerNotes.TIP: Tip names an end or point, rather than the whole leaf.

title: A Sunflower Facing the Garden
description: Look closely at a tall sunflower through its large flower head, small florets, and developing fruits.
cardDescription: Look closely at a tall sunflower through its large flower head, small florets, and developing fruits.
focus: A sunflower head contains many individual flowers. The outer rays and central disk florets have different forms, and the familiar edible seed is enclosed in a fruit wall.
solvingTip: Distinguish the whole head from one small flower or one developing fruit.
words: Tall daisy-family plant with a large familiar yellow-rayed head
One small individual flower within a sunflower head
Central region of a sunflower head containing many small florets

Broad green structure along a sunflower's stem
Edible inner part within a sunflower's hard fruit covering
Having considerable height, as many sunflowers do
Warm yellow color suggested by a bright sunflower border
Plant anchor extending into the soil below a sunflower
Unopened sunflower head before its florets expand
Whole flower cluster at the top of a sunflower stalk
Insect visiting the center of a sunflower

answerNotes.SUNFLOWER: A sunflower head is a cluster of many small flowers rather than one giant flower.
answerNotes.FLORET: Floret names one flower in the larger head; many disk florets can develop fruits.
answerNotes.DISK: The disk is the central area, while the showy rays appear around its edge.
answerNotes.RAY: A ray is a small flower form rather than simply a petal detached from one huge flower.
answerNotes.ACHENE: The familiar sunflower seed is botanically enclosed in a dry fruit wall; the fruit is commonly described as an achene or, more precisely in this family, a cypsela.

title: Autumn Mums at the Door
description: Explore familiar chrysanthemum displays through clustered flower heads, petal-like rays, and compact plant shapes.
cardDescription: Explore familiar chrysanthemum displays through clustered flower heads, petal-like rays, and compact plant shapes.
focus: Mums are chrysanthemums, a varied group with several flower forms. The clues describe the shape of a display and its component parts without assuming all varieties look alike.
solvingTip: Use the shape word or container first, then cross the less familiar flower-form terms.

answerNotes.MUMS: Mums is the familiar shortened plural; chrysanthemums have many flower shapes and colors.
answerNotes.POMPON: Pompon describes one compact flower form, not every chrysanthemum variety.
answerNotes.RAY: A ray is a type of small flower; the apparent head can contain many separate florets.
answerNotes.DISK: Some highly doubled forms conceal the disk, so it is not equally obvious in all varieties.
answerNotes.CUSHION: Cushion refers to growth shape rather than the material inside the container.

title: Bright Bracts on a Poinsettia
description: Examine a winter holiday plant through its colored bracts and the small flower structures at the center.
cardDescription: Examine a winter holiday plant through its colored bracts and the small flower structures at the center.
focus: The showy colored parts of a poinsettia are bracts rather than petals. The actual flowers are grouped in small central structures, while the plant itself is a shrub.
solvingTip: Look for whether the clue names a modified leaf, a flower cluster, or the entire plant.
words: Holiday plant known for colored bracts around small central flowers
Modified leaf giving a poinsettia much of its holiday color

Middle area containing a poinsettia's small flower groupings

answerNotes.POINSETTIA: The conspicuous red, cream, or pink parts are bracts, not large flower petals.
answerNotes.BRACT: A bract is associated with a flower or cluster; it differs from a petal within a flower's corolla.
answerNotes.CYATHIUM: A cyathium contains the tiny flowers; it is not the broad colored structure surrounding them.
answerNotes.SHRUB: Poinsettias are shrubs in suitable climates even when sold as small indoor plants.
answerNotes.SAP: Sap names the fluid rather than the colored plant parts or central flowers.

title: A Camellia Beside the Walk
description: Explore an evergreen flowering shrub through glossy leaves, rounded buds, and its garden setting.
cardDescription: Explore an evergreen flowering shrub through glossy leaves, rounded buds, and its garden setting.
focus: Camellias include species and varieties that flower at different times. The clues describe recognizable foliage and flower parts, while an evergreen habit concerns leaf retention rather than constant blooming.
solvingTip: Separate a leaf quality from a flowering stage or a shrub form.

answerNotes.CAMELLIA: Camellia includes several species and many varieties; flowering time is not the same for every kind.
answerNotes.EVERGREEN: Evergreen describes foliage retention, not a promise of flowers throughout the year.
answerNotes.GLOSSY: Glossy describes reflected light from the surface rather than a particular leaf color.
answerNotes.SEPAL: Sepals form the calyx, outside the petals; the names identify different flower parts.
answerNotes.SHRUB: A shrub describes a growth form rather than one exact maximum height.
